title: Diagnostic curettage (D&C)
what: The doctor takes the inner lining of the uterus for testing. It is done under short general anesthesia, often together with a camera look inside the uterus, called hysteroscopy.
why: To find the cause of bleeding from the uterus, or for polyps or a thick uterine lining seen on ultrasound.
duration: the procedure usually takes 15 to 30 minutes; you often go home the same day
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. The doctor will tell you what to stop and when
Heart or lung disease, or diabetes
If you or your relatives ever had problems with anesthesia

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood tests, a smear, and sometimes an ECG. Your clinic will give you the list.

prepare.title: Timing
prepare.text: The doctor usually picks the date based on your cycle. Confirm it in advance.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no food for 6 to 8 hours and no drinks for a few hours before. Your clinic will give you the exact time.

prepare.title: Hygiene
prepare.text: Take a shower in the morning. Do not douche or use suppositories unless your doctor told you to.

bring: Someone to go with you. You cannot drive after anesthesia
steps: You change into a gown, and a cannula is put into a vein
You lie in the gynecology chair
The anesthesiologist gives the medicine, and you fall asleep
The doctor widens the cervix and gently takes tissue
The tissue is sent to the lab
You wake up and rest while staff watch you
feel: A pulling pain in the lower belly, like period cramps. You will get pain medicine
after: Bloody discharge usually lasts a few days, sometimes up to 10 days
Usually for 2 weeks: no sex, tampons, baths, swimming pools, or saunas. Check with your doctor
Do not drive on the day of anesthesia
Tissue results usually come in 1 to 2 weeks. Your doctor will explain them
red_flags: Heavy bleeding that soaks a pad in 1 hour
A fever over 38 degrees, or belly pain that gets worse
Fainting or severe weakness: call emergency services right away

faq.a: No, it is done under short general anesthesia. Afterwards your belly may ache, like during a period.

faq.q: How long does discharge last after a D&C?
faq.a: Usually a few days, sometimes up to 10 days. If bleeding is heavy or you have a fever, see a doctor.

reminders.text: Procedure tomorrow. Bring your ID, test results, pads, and someone to go with you. Eat and drink only until the time your clinic gave you.
